thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GeoDNS probe failures detected for eu-west1 region. health-check-fail rate > 40% across probes. Severity: P1. Auto-page sent to #incidents and on-call group. Incident page: https://redwood.app/incidents/6278912345

alex.sre: seeing a surge of 502/504 from EU customers, rolling window 2m. Quick dig from our probe:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.14-Ubuntu <<>> www.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; ANSWER SECTION:
www.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 203.0.113.45
;; Query time: 612 msec
;; SERVER: 8.8.8.8#53(8.8.8.8)
```

mira.net: our internal resolver probes (eu-west) show timeouts and stale cache hits. TTL alignment looks off between Route53 and Cloudflare (CF returning old A record with high TTL). Example: CF edge returned TTL=3600, Route53 returned TTL=60. Could be propagation or resolver cache-flapping.

dave-sre: ok. hypothesis: upstream resolver probe noise + Route53 latency causing GeoDNS library to mark endpoints unhealthy (debouncing logic firing). If geodns marks eu pool unhealthy it bounces requests and causes mid-flight failures. Fix plan: reduce Route53 TTL to 30s, tombstone eu pool weight to force fallback to global pool, and enable probe backoff adjustments. Rolling steps: 1) lower TTL 2) set weight 0 for geo-eu record 3) update probe debounce window to 120s while we stabilize

alex.sre: I'll run the Route53 change (low risk, quick revert). Pushing now.
```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1234567 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"www.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"geo-eu","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"203.0.113.45"}]}}]}'
```

infra-bot: Deploy log: route53-upsert job queued by alex.sre (run-id: r-9923).

mira.net: contacted Cloudflare support with debug traces (ticket CF-2026-881). CF acknowledges increased 5xx from their EU edge at ~12:32 UTC. They recommend switching traffic to another pool while they investigate edge cache invalidation.

priya-support: customer impact: ~1.8% of requests in EU reported 502/504, support queue has 6 open high-priority tickets referencing session failures. No data exfiltration or authentication issues. ETA for initial mitigation: 15 min.

dave-sre: weight change applied, TTL lowered. Now setting geodns fallback policy to prefer global pool. Running probes...

alex.sre: probe output after change:
```
GET https://probe-eu1.redwood.ai/health -> 200 OK (latency 120ms)
GET https://probe-eu2.redwood.ai/health -> 200 OK (latency 98ms)
Resolver probe: successful resolution to global-primary IP 198.51.100.12
```

mira.net: we're seeing resolver error rate drop to 4% on eu probes. CF ticket updated; they are reprocessing edge caches.

priya-support: confirming customer-facing metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 2.1% -> 0.2% in EU within 3 minutes of the weight change. Support notified customers on the incidents status page. :thumbsup:

alex.sre: opened AWS support case with Route53 (case #5122331) to confirm if they observed increased latency on the authoritative nameservers for eu subdelegations.

dave-sre: action item: revert TTL to baseline 300s after stabilization window (2 hours), and run a controlled gradual rollback of geodns weights rather than abrupt flip. Also adjust the debounce thresholds in our probe config from 60s->120s to avoid oscillation.

infra-bot: pager reminder scheduled for handoff in 45m to night shift.

mira.net: added a temporary internal dashboard panel: geodns-resolve-latency (eu), route53-query-time (eu-auth), cf-edge-5xx(eu). Share link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/geo-resolve/6278912345

priya-support: support summary for external comms:
- Impact: intermittent 502/504 for EU customers (peak 2.1% of requests), ongoing mitigation in place.
- Mitigation: geo-eu pool weight set to 0; TTL lowered to 30s to accelerate failover; Cloudflare engaged (ticket CF-2026-881).
- Next update: 30m or when full recovery observed.

dave-sre: logging final technical notes in incident tracker. Leaving a short runbook addendum: "If resolver probe flapping detected, prefer tombstone weight + low TTL instead of immediate failover to avoid split-brain between authoritative providers. Increase probe debounce to 2x for 30m window."

karen-nightshift: taking handoff. Received summary and links. I'll monitor eu probes, Cloudflare ticket, and support queue overnight. My phone: +1-555-0199.

alex.sre: thanks Karen. I'll stay reachable until stabilization. If anything regresses, revert weight to previous and escalate with Route53/CF contacts. :eyes:

oncall-bot: Incident updated: mitigations applied. Current severity: P1 -> P2 (monitoring). Next update scheduled 30 minutes. Incident record: https://redwood.app/incidents/6278912345

karen-nightshift: acknowledged. Handing off to night. Action items carried: (1) monitor geodns-resolve-latency and cf-edge-5xx, (2) follow up with AWS/CF support for root cause, (3) revert TTL/weights after stabilization window if clean.

priya-support: will coordinate customer comms and post a brief status to status.redwood.ai once we confirm full recovery.
